pr_title: fix(common): parse `YYYY-MM` strings as UTC dates
pr_body:
In 2aba8b0 we fixed the DatePipe so that when it parsed date strings
that looked like `YYYY-MM-DD` it created a UTC date that was not
affected by the local timezone of the JavaScript engine.

This commit does the same for date strings of the form `YYYY-MM`
and `YYYY`.

Fixes #33944

issue_context.title: DatePipe treats ISO-8601 YYYY-MM format as a date-time and adds timezone
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package @angular/common ### Is this a regression? No ### Description I am trying to use the `DatePipe` with a string input that is in the ISO-8601 Year and Month format `YYYY-MM`. The DatePipe doc states that it supports ISO-8601 strings: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/8.2.14/packages/common/src/pipes/date_pipe.ts#L160 The `DatePipe` incorrectly assumes the date is in GMT time. Then the resulting output is converted to the user's locale, which can cause off-by-1-day errors depending on your timezone. E.g. `{{"2019-02" | date:'MMM. yyyy'}}` Expected: `Feb. 2019` Actual: `Jan. 2019` I don't see the same issue when using the other ISO-8601 format `YYYY-MM-DD`, there is a specific piece of code to handle timezone offsets for it: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/8.2.14/packages/common/src/i18n/format_date.ts#L675. I think it should also apply to the `YYYY-MM` format. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-jh7xqs ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 

Angular: 8.2.9
... animations, bazel, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core
... forms, platform-browser, platform-browser-dynamic, router
comments: This looks like a valid bug. Here is where it was fixed for full dates: https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/2aba8b0ff2c5d6979802b96842aceccad3d5716d

@pearlsze - I can no longer reproduce this. I can't see anything that has changed in the codebase to fix this. But then I wonder if there is something about the local timezone that makes the difference. Can you reproduce it with the latest Angular?

@petebacondarwin Hi, I made a new [stackblitz](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-v1ddqc?file=src/app/app.component.html) with the latest angular 11.1.1, and still see the issue.

The output I see (with the first one being incorrect). 
```
With YYYY-MM format
Input: 2019-02
Output: Jan. 2019

Specifying pipe to use 'GMT' timezone
Input: 2019-02
Output: Feb. 2019

With YYYY-MM-DD format
Input: 2019-02-01
Output: Feb. 2019

```

@pearlsze what timezone are you in? I am in London UK (GMT) and I don't see `Jan. 2019` I see `Feb. 2019`.
I tried overriding the timezone in Chrome but whatever time-zone I choose I get the same result.
@petebacondarwin I am in PST! Using the location override in Chrome (assuming you are too), "San Francisco" reproduces the issue, but for "London" I no longer see the issue.
Hmm, I tried "Mountain View"... let me try again.

OK!

In my local timezone `new Date('2019-02')` gives me `Fri Feb 01 2019 00:00:00 GMT+0000 (Greenwich Mean Time)`
And in San Francisco timezone `new Date('2019-02')` gives me `Thu Jan 31 2019 16:00:00 GMT-0800 (Pacific Standard Time)`
